title: Digital Identity for Nations: Unlinkability, Subsidiarity and Interop
description: Drawing on the digital identity work done, and still ongoing, with the European Decentralisation Institute, I’ll start with the basics (eID, levels of assurance, credentials, wallets) and map today’s Cambrian explosion of identity systems in Europe and globally. Read as DPI, a system can be active and cross-sector yet still concentrate control. The question isn’t whether identity systems harmonise across borders, but on what terms. I’ll argue the credible route to global interoperability is a trust framework grounded in mutual recognition, digital subsidiarity, open standards, and unlinkability-by-default as a binding architectural requirement. I’ll show where Ethereum and blockchain-based features meet these needs, above all as a neutral verification layer for digital trust, and report on live cases such as Bhutan NDI, Taiwan TW DIW, Buenos Aires QuarkID and UAE Pass. I’ll close with a call to action to join the Pan-European Trust Framework.
abstract: A national identity system can qualify as digital public infrastructure and still be open to surveillance and capture. This talk argues subsidiarity and unlinkability-by-default are the credible route to a rights-based, globally interoperable trust framework. Attendees will get insights on digital identity as DPI and on Ethereum-based and other blockchain cases like Bhutan NDI. The talk will close with a call to action to join a multi-stakeholder initiative making it happen: the Pan-European Trust Framework (PETF).
